section_summary: This section covers correspondence and official documentation from 1947 to 1949 regarding Japanese passports and travel documents during the Allied Occupation of Japan under the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP). It includes despatches transmitting the withheld passports of Japanese embassy personnel repatriated from Europe via Sweden, as well as specimen copies of both the former Imperial and redesigned postwar Japanese passports conforming to SCAPIN 1609. It also details the establishment of standing operating procedures utilizing U.S. military attaches and the Department of the Army Civil Affairs Division to execute passport extensions and travel authorizations on behalf of SCAP for Japanese nationals traveling abroad.

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting the withheld Japanese passports of Yoshio Yamamoto and Naoe Sakai for delivery via official channels.
subfiles.from: John A. Birch, Attache, American Legation, Stockholm
subfiles.summary: Transmits the passports of Yoshio Yamamoto and Naoe Sakai, former Berlin embassy personnel repatriated via Sweden, for delivery in Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 353, Transmitting Passports of Japanese Nationals Repatriated to Japan

subfiles.about: Instruction forwarding the withheld passports of Yoshio Yamamoto and Naoe Sakai to Tokyo for delivery to the individuals.
subfiles.summary: Forwards passports of Yoshio Yamamoto and Naoe Sakai to the Political Adviser in Tokyo for delivery to the individuals.
subfiles.title: Instruction Regarding Delivery of Japanese Passports Withheld by Swedish Authorities
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting five specimen copies of Japanese passports incorporating new travel conditions authorized under SCAPIN 1609.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits specimen Japanese passports incorporating travel conditions authorized by SCAP directive SCAPIN 1609 for Japanese nationals permitted to travel abroad.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1014, Travel Documents for Japanese Nationals Traveling Abroad

subfiles.about: Cover sheet for specimen passport enclosures transmitted with Tokyo Despatch No. 1014.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet for specimen passports enclosed with Tokyo Despatch No. 1014.
subfiles.title: Enclosure Cover Sheet to Despatch No. 1014

subfiles.about: Specimen 32-page Imperial Japanese Government passport booklet modified to incorporate SCAPIN 1609 travel authorizations.
subfiles.from: Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan
subfiles.summary: A thirty-two page specimen passport booklet (No. 390572) issued under the Imperial Japanese Government for authorized travel abroad under SCAP directive SCAPIN 1609. The document includes bilingual Japanese and English identification provisions referencing SCAP authorization, alongside French diplomatic request text, personal description fields, notice conditions, and blank visa pages.
subfiles.title: Specimen Imperial Japanese Government Passport No. 390572

subfiles.about: Duplicate file copy of Despatch No. 1014 showing State Department receipt and correlation distribution markings.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Duplicate file copy of Despatch No. 1014 transmitting specimen passports issued to Japanese nationals under SCAPIN 1609.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1014, Travel Documents for Japanese Nationals Traveling Abroad (File Copy)

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting five specimen copies of the redesigned Japanese passport with revised format and wording.
subfiles.summary: Transmits five specimens of the redesigned Japanese passport, noting format changes including English and Japanese text only, omission of the Imperial crest, and removal of 'Imperial' from the government title.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1202, Transmitting Specimen Copies of New Japanese Passport

subfiles.about: Specimen copy of the redesigned blue 32-page Japanese Government passport omitting the Imperial crest and French text.
subfiles.from: Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan
subfiles.summary: A thirty-two page specimen of the revised Japanese Government passport booklet, featuring bilingual text in Japanese and English without French translations or the Imperial crest. It contains fields for bearer identification, personal description, SCAPIN 1609 travel authorization, validity renewal pages, and instructions governing passport invalidation.
subfiles.title: Specimen Japanese Government Passport

subfiles.about: Airgram requesting comments on a standard operating procedure allowing military attaches to extend Japanese passports abroad.
subfiles.summary: Inquires regarding a Military Attache procedure for extending passports of Japanese nationals abroad, requesting the State Department's comments.
subfiles.title: Airgram No. A-307, Procedure for Extending Passports of Japanese Nationals

subfiles.about: Instruction explaining Department of State concurrence with military attaches executing SCAP decisions on passport extensions.
subfiles.summary: Explains that military attaches act as SCAP agents for Japanese passport extensions because SCAP approval is indispensable and discretionary powers remain military.
subfiles.title: Instruction to Nanking, Extension of Japanese Travel Documents by Military Attaches

subfiles.about: Department of State charge slip recording the checkout of Circular Instruction 95-1 regarding Japanese nationals.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip recording the removal of Circular Instruction 95-1 regarding Japanese nationals from the files.
subfiles.title: Form DS-516 Charge Slip for Circular Instruction 95-1

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting SCAP memorandum establishing procedures for extending and amending Japanese passports abroad through military channels.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits a SCAP memorandum of November 12, 1948 outlining standard operating procedures for amending and extending Japanese passports abroad through military channels, citing precedents including Moral Rearmament delegates and Episcopal bishops.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 795, Amendment and Extension of Japanese Passports Issued Under SCAP Authorization

subfiles.about: SCAP memorandum establishing standard operating procedures for extending the validity and scope of passports of Japanese nationals temporarily abroad.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (GHQ SCAP)
subfiles.summary: Establishes standard procedures for extending the validity and scope of Japanese passports abroad, designating the U.S. Army Civil Affairs Division as SCAP's agent in the United States.
subfiles.title: Standing Operating Procedure for Extending Validity of Passports of Japanese Nationals while Temporarily Abroad
subfiles.to: Diplomatic Missions and Foreign Government Agencies in Japan
